rows: Days to a couple of weeks to learn platform basics, content calendars, and posting cadence.
A few months of managing a real account with a real audience before you can defend a content strategy with actual engagement or conversion data.
Everyone thinks they already know this from personal use, which is exactly why the entry-level pool is the most crowded.
A short stretch to learn structure, SEO-aware writing, and basic brief-following.
Several months to a year of writing for real briefs and real audiences before your writing reliably drives a measurable outcome, not just reads well.
Writing that sounds good and writing that converts are different skills, and only real audience feedback teaches the second one.

items.heading: Whether You Can Open Google
items.text: Whether you can open Google Ads Manager, GA4, or a CRM and produce a result without needing a tutorial mid-task.

items.heading: A Portfolio That States Outcomes
items.text: A portfolio that states outcomes ("reduced cost per lead from X to Y") rather than only activities ("managed a Rs 50,000/month budget").

items.heading: A Live Task
items.text: A live task or a short paid trial project, increasingly common in place of relying on certificates alone.

items.heading: Genuine Depth in At Least
items.text: Genuine depth in at least one channel, plus familiarity with the standard tools for that channel, not shallow exposure to all five.
